bug_description.normalized: Two inbound `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` updates cause wpantund to create a SLAAC unicast-address map entry, then remove the matching on-mesh prefix. `on_mesh_prefix_was_removed()` binds a reference to that map key, `unicast_address_was_removed()` erases the same `mUnicastAddresses` node, and the dangling reference is then passed into `TunnelIPv6Interface::remove_address()`, producing a heap-use-after-free read.

source.description: Earliest project-side parse on the witnessed path: it decodes the first attacker-controlled inbound Spinel frame into a header and callback command before any property-specific parsing happens.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is 38 bytes. Byte 0 is ASCII `1`, selecting `NCPInputFuzzTarget`. The remaining 37 bytes are streamed one byte at a time to the emulated NCP serial fd and contain two HDLC-delimited inbound Spinel frames. For the first relevant frame, after `ncp_to_driver_pump()` strips the HDLC delimiter and CRC trailer, this unpack reads `mInboundFrame` as a flagged Spinel callback with `command_value == SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_IS`; the later callback unpack at line 4731 decodes the same frame as `key == SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` with a non-empty value span.
source.note: This is earlier than the callback/property parse in `handle_ncp_spinel_callback()`: it is the first project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled serial frame and proves the vulnerable path begins with an inbound Spinel `PROP_VALUE_IS` update.

tainted_value_origin.var: prefix_addr, prefix_len, stable, flags, is_local, rloc16
tainted_value_origin.code: len = spinel_datatype_unpack(value_data_ptr, value_data_len, SPINEL_DATATYPE_STRUCT_S(SPINEL_DATATYPE_IPv6ADDR_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_UINT8_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_BOOL_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_UINT8_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_BOOL_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_UINT16_S), &prefix_addr, &prefix_len, &stable, &flags, &is_local, &rloc16);
tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete vulnerability-relevant state derived from input is the parsed ON_MESH_NETS entry fields: prefix bytes plus the flags and locality bits that decide whether wpantund inserts an NCP-origin on-mesh prefix and synthesizes a SLAAC address.

root_cause.description: The code aliases the `mUnicastAddresses` map key by reference instead of copying it. When the same map node is erased in `unicast_address_was_removed()`, this reference becomes dangling.
root_cause.note: The patch fixes exactly this line by changing the reference to a by-value copy (`struct in6_addr address = addr_iter->first;`), so the later erase no longer invalidates the object passed to `remove_address()`.

sink.description: ASAN crash site. `remove_address()` dereferences the pointer passed from `unicast_address_was_removed()`, but that pointer addresses the freed `mUnicastAddresses` map key.
sink.note: The sanitizer reports a heap-use-after-free READ of size 4 at this line, with the free originating from `mUnicastAddresses.erase(address)` in `unicast_address_was_removed()` and the allocation originating from `mUnicastAddresses[address] = entry` in `unicast_address_was_added()`.

parser_admitted.description: After the data pump and callback unpack decode a `PROP_VALUE_IS` frame for `SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS`, this dispatch enters the exact parser that adds the prefix on the first frame and removes it on the later empty frame.

poc.trigger: The staged witness file `poc` reproduces the saved ASAN crash. It selects `NCPInputFuzzTarget` with leading byte `1`, then streams two HDLC-delimited inbound Spinel `PROP_VALUE_IS` updates for `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS`: the first is non-empty and, on the witnessed run, creates an NCP-origin on-mesh SLAAC prefix plus its derived unicast address; the later frame decodes to an empty `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` value, which removes that prefix and drives the stale-reference path into `TunnelIPv6Interface::remove_address()`.

format.name: wpantund NCP input stream with HDLC-delimited Spinel `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` updates
format.contract: Byte 0 must be ASCII `1` so the harness chooses `NCPInputFuzzTarget`. The remaining bytes must include two inbound HDLC-delimited Spinel `PROP_VALUE_IS` frames for property `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS`: first a non-empty frame whose value decodes to a non-local `/64` on-mesh+SLAAC prefix entry, then a later frame whose decoded value span is empty (`value_data_len == 0`) so the earlier NCP-origin prefix is absent from the refreshed list and `handle_ncp_spinel_value_is_ON_MESH_NETS()` calls `on_mesh_prefix_was_removed()` on it.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled serial stream is HDLC-decoded into two inbound Spinel `PROP_VALUE_IS` callback frames that reach the `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` handlers.
The first `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` frame parses one non-local prefix entry and forwards it into on-mesh-prefix management.
wpantund inserts the parsed NCP-origin on-mesh prefix, takes the SLAAC branch, derives an address from the prefix, and stores that address in `mUnicastAddresses`.
A later empty `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` update copies the existing prefix set, skips the parse loop, and forwards the unmatched NCP-origin prefix to `on_mesh_prefix_was_removed()`.

The removal path erases the live prefix, finds the matching SLAAC unicast-address map entry, aliases its key by reference, and `unicast_address_was_removed()` frees that same map node before reusing the dangling reference.
The interface removal code dereferences the dangling `in6_addr *` argument, triggering the observed heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: After HDLC decoding and CRC stripping of the first relevant serial frame, this unpack materializes a flagged Spinel callback with `command_value == SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_IS` from attacker-controlled bytes.
For that `PROP_VALUE_IS` callback frame, the second unpack reads `key == SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` and a non-empty value span from the same inbound frame.
Property dispatch takes the `key == SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` branch and enters the vulnerable on-mesh-prefix parser with that non-empty value buffer.

fine_trace.var: prefix_addr, prefix_len, stable, flags, is_local, rloc16
fine_trace.code: len = spinel_datatype_unpack(value_data_ptr, value_data_len, SPINEL_DATATYPE_STRUCT_S(SPINEL_DATATYPE_IPv6ADDR_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_UINT8_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_BOOL_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_UINT8_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_BOOL_S SPINEL_DATATYPE_UINT16_S), &prefix_addr, &prefix_len, &stable, &flags, &is_local, &rloc16);
fine_trace.note: The first `THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` payload is unpacked into one prefix entry. On the witnessed run, `len > 0` and `is_local == false`, so the parsed prefix state is eligible for insertion as an NCP-origin on-mesh prefix.
The parsed prefix is inserted into the live `mOnMeshPrefixes` multimap as an NCP-origin entry, establishing state that the later empty update will remove.

Because the parsed entry is on-mesh, SLAAC, and `/64`, and no address with that prefix exists yet, wpantund derives a SLAAC unicast address from the attacker-selected prefix and the local MAC address.
The derived SLAAC address is stored as a key in `mUnicastAddresses`. ASAN's allocation stack identifies this assignment as the allocation site of the map node later freed and re-read.

Later bytes on the same witness stream form a second inbound frame; after HDLC decoding and CRC stripping, this unpack materializes another flagged Spinel callback with `command_value == SPINEL_CMD_PROP_VALUE_IS`.

depends_on.via: later bytes from the same attacker-controlled serial stream

fine_trace.note: For this later frame, the callback unpack yields `key == SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` and `value_data_len == 0`; after HDLC/CRC removal the frame payload is just `80 06 5A`.
Property dispatch again takes the `key == SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS` branch, but this time it enters the parser with an empty value span.

On the second invocation, `on_mesh_prefixes` starts as a copy of current `mOnMeshPrefixes`, so it contains the NCP-origin prefix inserted at step 5. Because step 9 produced `value_data_len == 0`, the parse loop is skipped and that copied entry remains unmatched for cleanup.
The cleanup loop walks the unmatched copied entry and passes its preserved prefix, length, flags, stability, and RLOC into `on_mesh_prefix_was_removed()`.

Inside `on_mesh_prefix_was_removed()`, the live `mOnMeshPrefixes` entry matching the copied prefix/entry is found and erased. This makes the later `!has_slaac_on_mesh_prefix(prefix)` test true for that `/64` prefix.

With no remaining SLAAC on-mesh entry for that prefix, the removal path searches `mUnicastAddresses` for the matching NCP-origin address and gets an iterator to the existing map node created at step 7.
Instead of copying the IPv6 address bytes out of the map node, the code binds `address` as a reference directly to `addr_iter->first`, aliasing storage owned by the `mUnicastAddresses` node.
Before deleting the node, the removal path copies its metadata into local `entry`, preserving `entry.get_prefix_len()` for the later interface-removal call even after the key storage is freed.

Erasing the `mUnicastAddresses` entry frees the map node that owns `addr_iter->first`, so the referenced `address` object from step 15 becomes dangling. ASAN's free stack points to this exact statement.

Because the origin is `kOriginThreadNCP`, the function forwards `&address` to the primary interface after step 17. That converts the dangling reference into a dangling pointer argument while `entry.get_prefix_len()` stays valid from step 16.
The interface-removal sink immediately dereferences the stale `addr` pointer passed from step 18. ASAN reports the resulting heap-use-after-free READ of size 4 at this line.
